scenarios.title: The Rookie Injury
scenarios.text: Your first pro injury, a strained hip flexor, and the trainers are talking about you like a part that might not fit back in. You can hear them through the curtain.

choices.label: Do the rehab exactly
choices.result: Every exercise the trainers give you gets done on time, and nothing extra. You're back a week early, and the head trainer starts using you as an example.

choices.label: Push to come back early
choices.result: Kicking before the trainers clear you gets you back on time, and sore for a month. You never quite trust your hip on cold mornings after that.

choices.label: Ask how the veterans came back
choices.result: Each veteran has a comeback story, and one has a stretch that works. By the end of the week you're doing it in the hallway with three of them.

choices.label: Use what you learned before
choices.result: You've done a long rehab before, so you build the plan with the trainers instead of waiting for one. They're impressed, and you're back early.
choices.lock_text: having been through a hard recovery before

scenarios.title: Summer at Home
scenarios.text: Your first offseason back home. Everyone at the grocery store wants to talk about one kick, the high school has your picture in the trophy case, and {parent} has told the whole street you're coming.

choices.label: Enjoy being home
choices.result: Your old bedroom, {parent}'s cooking and {sibling} in the next room, just like before. The town makes a fuss, you let it, and it's the best month you've had in a year.

choices.label: Train at your old high school
choices.result: You train on your old high school field every morning. The kids on the team start showing up to watch.

choices.label: Hide from the attention
choices.result: You stay in, see {best_friend} and a few old friends at night, and avoid the grocery store entirely. It's quiet and restful, and by July it's a little lonely.

scenarios.title: The Veteran's Advice
scenarios.text: An eleven-year veteran pulls you aside after practice, sits you on a bench by the field and says he has a few rules for surviving the league, if you're smart enough to want them.

choices.label: Write them down tonight
choices.result: Every rule goes in a notebook that night. Some are about kicking; most are about money, agents and who to trust. You reread them every season after.

choices.label: Ask about his worst season
choices.result: His worst season comes out over an hour on that bench: the cut, the divorce, the comeback. You learn more from the story than from any rule.

choices.label: Nod and forget them
choices.result: Nodding politely gets you to dinner on time, and you forget the rules by dessert. Three of them come back to you later, the hard way.

scenarios.title: The First Media Interview
scenarios.text: Local reporters catch you at your locker on your second day, before anyone has taught you what not to say. There are four microphones, and one of them is very close to your face.

choices.label: Keep it boring
choices.result: Short, polite answers and nothing quotable. The story that runs is boring, which {coach} likes, and your agent sends you a thumbs-up you didn't expect.

choices.label: Be yourself
choices.result: You joke, tell a story about your college holder and admit you're nervous. The reporters like you, and so do the fans.

choices.label: Say something bold
choices.result: You say you'll be the best kicker in the league in three years. It's the headline, and the veterans tape it to your locker.

scenarios.title: The Missed Opportunity
scenarios.text: A bad practice in front of the whole staff: three misses in a row from your favorite spot, the general manager watching from the sideline. By lunch someone in the building is asking about your roster spot.

choices.label: Find out what the staff saw
choices.result: {coach} pulls up the practice film after lunch and freezes it on your plant foot. It's a timing issue, and fixable, and you breathe properly for the first time all day.

choices.label: Kick until the lights come on
choices.result: Long after everyone leaves, you're still out there, kicking until it feels right again. The groundskeeper finally turns the lights on for you and doesn't say a word.

choices.label: Leave it at the facility
choices.result: One practice doesn't define a season, you decide, and you leave it at the facility. Tomorrow is better, mostly, though the general manager's face stays with you on the drive home.

scenarios.title: The Agent Calls
scenarios.text: Your agent calls on a Tuesday night to talk about your contract, your future and a few things you'd rather not hear, starting with the list of reasons rookies get cut before October.

choices.label: Listen to all of it
choices.result: The whole list, start to finish, without interrupting once. It's sobering to hear out loud, and by the end you know exactly which mistakes you're never going to make.

choices.label: Ask for a two-year plan
choices.result: A real plan for the next two years arrives in your inbox by Friday, in writing, with dates. It's the first time your career has looked like something you can steer.

choices.label: Cut the call short
choices.result: Kicking is all you want to think about, so the call ends early. Your agent sends the list by email anyway, and you read it at two in the morning.

scenarios.title: The First Endorsement
scenarios.text: A local car wash offers you your first sponsorship: a billboard by the highway, four appearances in a giant foam sponge costume and a check that's small, but yours.

choices.label: Sign with the car wash
choices.result: The billboard goes up by the highway a week later, a little blurry, and every teammate sends you a photo of it. The holder sets it as his phone background.

choices.label: Ask your agent first
choices.result: Your agent negotiates the appearances down to two and the check up by half. The owner still makes you wear the sponge costume once, and you secretly love it.

choices.label: Keep your weeks clear
choices.result: No billboard, no sponge suit, no appearances. Your weeks stay clear for kicking, your account stays the same, and the car wash signs a local weatherman instead.

scenarios.title: The Old Friend's Request
scenarios.text: {best_friend} calls from home on a Sunday night and asks you for money. It's quiet for a long time before they ask, and you can hear how much it costs them to say it.

choices.label: Send it that night
choices.result: The money is in {best_friend}'s account before you hang up, and you never ask what it's for. They cry on the phone, and so, after the call, do you.

choices.label: Ask what it's for
choices.result: It's rent, three months behind. Paying the landlord directly makes both of you feel better, and {best_friend} sends you a photo of the receipt with a heart on it.

choices.label: Say no kindly
choices.result: No, as kindly as you can manage. It's true and it isn't, and the next phone call with {best_friend} is shorter, and the one after that doesn't come.

scenarios.title: The Long-Distance Relationship
scenarios.text: {love_interest} is three states away, and your schedule doesn't have room for flights. Your calls have started ending with long silences neither of you knows how to fill.

choices.label: Fly them in for the bye
choices.result: A flight for the bye week, booked that night. It's short, and it's enough until the next one, and you both cry at the airport.

choices.label: Call every night at ten
choices.result: A video call every night at ten, no matter what. Some nights it's five minutes and a yawn, and it holds.

choices.label: Put the season first
choices.result: The season comes first, you explain, and you'll make it up in the offseason. {love_interest} says okay, too quickly, and hangs up first.

scenarios.title: The Coach's Criticism
scenarios.text: {coach} tells you, in front of the specialists, that your preparation isn't professional yet. The punter suddenly studies the floor, and {holder} won't look at you.

choices.label: Ask for specifics
choices.result: Three specific things, you ask for, and {coach} lists them on a whiteboard: film, sleep, and the way you warm up. By November you've done all three, and the coach notices.

choices.label: Show up an hour earlier
choices.result: An hour earlier every day for a month, and you never mention why. {coach} never mentions it either, but your name moves to the top of the practice sheet.

choices.label: Push back
choices.result: Your preparation got you here, you point out. The specialists go very quiet, {holder} gives you a look that says 'not now', and {coach} walks away mid-sentence.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Mistake
scenarios.text: At the team's charity gala, you trip over a cable in front of a dessert table, take the whole thing down with you, and come up wearing a cheesecake. Three cameras catch every second.

choices.label: Laugh at yourself
choices.result: Laughing first saves you. You help clean up, then post the clip yourself with a caption about your leg strength. It's the most popular thing you've ever posted.

choices.label: Pay for the desserts
choices.result: The organizers get an apology and a check for the desserts before the night is over. They're touched, and the event coordinator invites you back to run the dessert table next year.

choices.label: Hope nobody saw
choices.result: Slipping out early doesn't help: the veterans saw, and they leave a slice of cheesecake in your locker every week for the rest of the season. You spend the night at the kicking net.

scenarios.title: The First Charity Event
scenarios.text: The club sends you to a community center's reading day, alone, with a box of picture books and no instructions. Twenty kids sit on a rug, waiting to see what a kicker is for.

choices.label: Read to the kids
choices.result: Sitting on the floor, you read three books in terrible voices, including a very dramatic dragon. The kids demand a fourth, and one of them asks for your autograph on her shoe.

choices.label: Talk about school
choices.result: How hard school was, and why you kept going: you tell them all of it, simply. A teacher finds you afterward and says one boy in the back needed exactly that.

choices.label: Sign and leave on time
choices.result: Autographs, a smile, a group photo, and you're out on time. It's perfectly fine and nobody remembers it, including you, by the following week.

scenarios.title: The Social Media Post
scenarios.text: An old post from college resurfaces the week your name starts showing up in the papers. It's not terrible, but it's not who you are now, and a fan account has just shared it to fifty thousand people.

choices.label: Delete it and apologize
choices.result: Deleted, then a short apology in your own words, no statement from a publicist. It fades in a day, and two teammates text that they respected how you handled it.

choices.label: Leave it up
choices.result: Silence, and the post stays up. It keeps resurfacing every time your name trends, for a month, and the club's media staff starts sighing when you walk past.

choices.label: Get the media staff's help
choices.result: The club's media staff walks you through it in ten minutes, calmly, like they've done it a hundred times. Nobody remembers the post by Friday.

choices.label: Do what worked before
choices.result: This has happened before, so you know the steps: delete, two honest sentences, practice. It's over by lunch, and the media staff asks if you want a job.
choices.lock_text: having handled an old post the right way before
